title: work handed to a node reaches no surface that node reads: the register can record an assignment and cannot deliver one
body:
**THE SURFACE WAS INDEXED THE WHOLE TIME, AND INDEXING IS NOT THE FIX.** Work handed to a node reaches no surface that node reads. The register can record an assignment and has no way to deliver one.

## The measured instance

`0175` said in its prose *handed to ic as surface owner*. **It reached neither ic's board nor any inbox** -- live or archived, both checked -- and sat undelivered for five days. **The consequence is on the record rather than hypothetical: cc independently re-filed the same defect as `0239`, and fixed it.** A duplicate is what an undelivered handover looks like from outside.

## The obvious explanation is REFUTED, which is what makes this its own defect

Not a reachability or a search problem:

```
intent search 'handed to ic as surface owner'  ->  intent/.canon/issues/0175.json   FIRST RESULT
```

**The assignment was findable from the day it was written.** What is missing is a reason to look: nobody queries 250-odd issue bodies for their own name, and there is no field to filter on. **A searchable surface with no query anyone would think to run.**

Driven 2026-09-05, both buckets, so the enumeration is not incomplete by construction the way an earlier one was (it was taken from a single OPEN row, which cannot carry `closed`):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| fields on a CLOSED issue | `body, closed, created, number, reporter, schema, severity, slug, status, title` |
| fields on an OPEN issue | the same, less `closed` |
| filters `issues list` offers | `--kind open\|closed\|all`, and nothing else |

**No assignee. No owner. No notification.**

## NOT the whiteboard-indexing defect, and conflating them is the specific hazard

cc lost a measurement of their own the same week, and the two look like one seam from opposite ends. They are not. **The whiteboard is genuinely outside the index:**

```
intent search 'RUN THE VERBS'  ->  158 results, ZERO under intent/whiteboard/
grep -rl 'RUN THE VERBS' intent/whiteboard/*/wip.md  ->  cc, dc, hv, ic     (positive control)
```

**The discriminator eliminates staleness**, which would otherwise explain the whole result: `frobnicator` is on disk in exactly two files -- ic's board and `0244.json`, written within the same hour -- and the search returns the canon row and not the board. Same word, same tree, same moment; only the file differs.

**And the sharpest statement of it is vc's:** the one line in those 158 results mentioning a whiteboard at all is `ST0056/14`'s own title. **The only whiteboard the index can see is the work package for indexing whiteboards.**

**SO THE REMEDIES DO NOT CROSS.** An owner field fixes this row and does nothing for cc's -- their measurement would still sit in an unindexed file. Indexing the whiteboard fixes cc's and does nothing for this one -- the assignment here was already indexed. **A design treating them as one seam ships half a fix and reads as complete, which is `0257`'s shape one level up: a remedy that names both cases and reaches one is a wired-but-wrong remedy at the design level.**

cc's half already has a home and is deliberately not filed: `ST0056/14`, *Coordination model: whiteboard and inboxes in the store*, Not Started, scope L. Re-driven rather than taken on report.

## NOT `0208` either, and the distinction changes what a fix must contain

`0208` is AUTHORSHIP -- five nodes writing one tree under one git identity, so for a content file there is no mechanical answer to which node wrote it. This row is ASSIGNMENT -- who a piece of work is FOR, and how they would ever learn.

dc's finding belongs to `0208` and bears on this one: **`reporter` holds the human's git identity**, measured across all 227 issues at the time -- 187 `Matthew Sinclair`, 40 `matts`, nothing else -- so the register carries no node identity in EITHER direction. **Consequence for whoever designs this: an owner field is this row and an author field is `0208`, and a design adding only one fixes half while reading as complete.**

## Deliberately NOT stating the fix

*Issues need an owner field* is one candidate remedy, and filing it as the title would presuppose it. **The requirement is that work handed to a node reaches a surface that node reads at pickup** -- an owner field plus a filter is one way, a routed inbox entry is another, a store-side assignment event is a third. The protocol's own ruling is the general form and it is already written down for the `hv` inbox: **a write surface with no named reader is a queue, not a channel** -- and here it is worse, because the surface is not even a channel, it is a sentence in a document.

**SIZE UNMEASURED.** Nothing here costs a design that has not been chosen.

Filed by ic on vc's ruling (2026-09-05), after searching `assignment channel`, `owner field`, `assignee`, `no way to filter issues by owner` and `which node filed`. Only `0175` (the instance) and `0208` (the adjacent authorship row) came back.



## SIZED (ic, 2026-09-05, on vc's assignment). **THE TWO HALVES HAVE DIFFERENT SIZES AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THIS ROW'S SUBJECT.**

**THE CANDIDATES ARE PRICED, NOT CHOSEN.** This row declined to state the fix and that stands; a sizing that picked one would presuppose it by the back door.

### Half one -- the RECORD. Size **S**, and it needs NO migration

`Issue` in `model.rs:1889`. **The precedent is already in the struct and it is documented in `severity`'s own doc comment**, which exists because this exact question was answered once: an optional field is `Option<String>`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`, **validated at the DOOR and read permissively**, so a store written before the field existed stays readable.

**THAT IS WHY THE ~250 EXISTING ROWS COST NOTHING.** `severity` was added under exactly this rule and its own note records the measurement -- 165 issues across six estates, none to migrate.

| site | what changes |
| --- | --- |
| `model.rs` | one `Option<String>` field |
| `facade.rs` | `issue_add` / `issue_edit` signatures |
| `render.rs` | dispatch-table flag, parse, door validation, display column |
| `show.rs`, `mcp.rs` | one field each |
| GraphQL face | **free** -- derived via `SimpleObject` |

**TWO HAZARDS, BOTH ON THE RECORD ALREADY:**

1. **`render.rs` IS cc's FILE.** Announce before touching it. Most of this half lives there.
2. **A FLAG CAN SHIP DECLARED AND UNPARSED, AND THIS EXACT FIELD DID IT.** `render.rs:6727`, verbatim: *the table has declared `critical|high|medium|low` all along and `--help` printed it, but nothing parsed it -- `--severity bogus` exited 0 and wrote `bogus` into canon.* **A test that reads `--help` would have passed throughout.** Any `--owner` needs a test that DRIVES the flag and reads the stored value back. This is `0175`'s own defect class -- declared, not wired -- one level down.

### Half two -- DELIVERY. **UNSIZED, BECAUSE IT IS A DESIGN CHOICE, AND IT IS THE ACTUAL REQUIREMENT**

**THE RECORD HALF DOES NOT SATISFY THIS ROW AND MUST NOT BE MISTAKEN FOR IT.** An owner field plus an `--owner` filter makes the query POSSIBLE; it does not make anyone run it. **That is verbatim the diagnosis above -- a searchable surface with no query anyone would think to run.** Shipping half one alone converts *findable by a search nobody runs* into *findable by a filter nobody runs*, which is this row's own definition of the defect, not its fix.

**MEASURED: `pickup` reads BOARDS AND INBOXES AND NOTHING ELSE.** There is no issue query anywhere in the pickup path, so nothing a node reads at pickup can currently carry an assignment.

| candidate | delivery guaranteed by | size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** field + filter + the protocol tells nodes to run it at pickup | **discipline** -- a step in a skill | **S** on top of half one |
| **B.** the assignment ALSO writes a routed inbox entry | **mechanism** -- pickup already reads inboxes | **M**, and see the collision |
| **C.** a store-side assignment event | **mechanism** | **gated behind L** |

**A IS THE CHEAPEST AND THE WEAKEST**, and its weakness is the one this estate keeps re-learning: a write surface with no named reader is a queue, not a channel. A instructs a reader into existence and nothing enforces it.

**B COLLIDES WITH AN ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARY AND THE COLLISION IS THE INTERESTING PART.** The whiteboard is FILES; the register is the STORE. An issue verb writing `<node>/inbox.<sender>.md` would be the store reaching out to author a disk file, which is a direction that does not currently exist -- `st attach` writes store and canon and never the disk file. **So B is not "M plus plumbing"; it is M plus a boundary ruling that is not mine to make.**

**C IS THE CLEAN ONE AND IT IS NOT AVAILABLE YET.** It needs the whiteboard in the store, which is `ST0056/14` -- *Coordination model: whiteboard and inboxes in the store*, **Not Started, scope L**. C is therefore free-ish AFTER `ST0056/14` and unavailable before it.

### What this sizing says, in one line

**THE CHEAP HALF IS S AND FIXES NOTHING ON ITS OWN; THE HALF THAT FIXES IT IS A ROUTING DECISION WHOSE COST IS DOMINATED BY WHERE THE WHITEBOARD LIVES.** Anyone pricing this as "add an owner field" has priced the half that is not the subject.

**AND `ST0056/14`'s STATE IS THE REAL DEPENDENCY**, which makes the sequencing question -- *is this waiting for the whiteboard to move into the store, or is it worth an interim mechanism* -- the decision this row now needs. That is hv's, not mine, and it is the only thing this sizing leaves open.
